about: I am a Ph.D. student at the University of Campinas (Unicamp), working in the Laboratory of Security and Cryptography (LASCA) under the supervision of Prof. Hilder Lima.

Previously, I earned my M.Sc. and B.Sc. degrees from the Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC) under the supervision of Prof. Ricardo Custódio, where I was a member of the Laboratory of Computer Security (LabSEC).

My main research focuses on Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), a technology centered on preserving data privacy during computation. Specifically, I work on reducing the bootstrapping cost of FHE schemes from a theoretical perspective. During my Master's, I also researched applications of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and theoretical aspects aimed at strengthening the security of isogeny-based cryptographic schemes. More broadly, I am interested in cryptographic primitives studied from an algebraic point of view.
